_schema.intent: Declarative compatibility rules for (model, hardware, precision, ngpus) combinations the calc can emit. compute() stays pure physics/math; this layer captures kernel-availability and HF-repo-existence facts that the analytical model doesn't see. Rules are evaluated by src/compatibility.mjs::validate() and returned as { errors, warns }. The ui.mjs copy-button is gated on errors.

predicate_vocabulary.weight_prec: array of weight precisions the rule fires on (e.g. ["INT8"])
predicate_vocabulary.kv_prec: array of KV-cache precisions the rule fires on
predicate_vocabulary.act_prec: array of activation precisions the rule fires on
predicate_vocabulary.gpu_arch: array of hardware.arch values (turing | ada | ampere | ampere_dc | hopper)
predicate_vocabulary.gpu_fp8_tflops_null: boolean: true means rule fires when the selected hardware has no FP8 path (hw.fp8_tflops === null)
predicate_vocabulary.model_moe: boolean: true means rule fires on MoE models; false means dense-only
predicate_vocabulary.model_quant_variants_missing: string: rule fires when the model's quant_variants array does NOT contain this token (e.g. "AWQ")
predicate_vocabulary.ngpus_lt: rule fires when input.ngpus < this number
predicate_vocabulary.ngpus_gt: rule fires when input.ngpus > this number
predicate_vocabulary.isl_plus_osl_gt_model_max_context: boolean: rule fires when ISL+OSL > model.max_context
predicate_vocabulary.weight_act_prec_mismatch_non_fp8: boolean: fires when weight_prec ≠ act_prec AND not both FP8 (i.e. config silently rides FP16 compute path)

_schema.match_semantics: A rule fires only if EVERY key in its `when` block matches. Mismatched/missing input fields don't match. Severity is either "error" (gates the copy button) or "warn" (advisory only).
_schema.suggest_block: Optional. Free-form key/value hints rendered as the 'Try:' line under the reason. Keys mirror input field names (weight_prec, kv_prec, ngpus) plus a free-form 'note' string.

rules.reason: INT8 via bitsandbytes dequantizes weights every forward pass on non-Hopper GPUs — there is no fast INT8 kernel. Expect TBT far above the predicted value.

suggest.note: AWQ (INT4) has a Marlin kernel on Ampere+ and pre-quantized HF repos for most popular models.

rules.reason: INT8 works on Hopper but FP8 is the faster native tensor-core path.
Selected GPU has no hardware FP8 path. vLLM will reject the config or fall back to slow emulation.

suggest.note: Or AWQ (INT4) for a real memory saving with a fast kernel on Ampere+.

rules.reason: AWQ (INT4) requires a pre-quantized HuggingFace repo; the selected model has no community AWQ variant.
AWQ Marlin kernel requires sm_80+ (Ampere or later). On Turing (T4) AWQ falls back to a slow dequant path.
FP8 KV cache requires Ampere or later; Turing has no FP8 KV support in vLLM.
vLLM does not implement INT8 KV cache. Only FP8 (e5m2 / e4m3) and FP16/BF16 KV are real.
MoE models need ≥8 GPUs for reasonable expert distribution; per-GPU capacity for the expert pool is otherwise too small.
ISL+OSL exceeds the model's trained max_context — vLLM will reject requests at this length.

suggest.note: Reduce ISL or OSL, or pick a model with longer context.

rules.reason: vLLM uses the paired FP8 weight+activation tensor-core path only when both are FP8. Mismatched precisions silently ride the FP16 compute roofline — predicted throughput will overestimate.

suggest.note: Set act_prec = weight_prec, or accept the FP16 compute path.
